---
title: "Data sources and availability"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
# The helpers below query the live Dataverse collection, so the code is shown
# but not run when the site is built.
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = FALSE)
```

G-TROPIC combines five published sources into exposure tables for every
second-level administrative unit (ADM2) and every storm in the International
Best Track Archive for Climate Stewardship (IBTrACS) since 1980. This article
describes those sources, when they are updated, and how to see what is
available before you query.

## Sources

| Source | Provides | Updates and coverage |
| --- | --- | --- |
| IBTrACS | storm tracks, identifiers, names and intensities, from which wind exposure and storm distances are derived | raw data on Sundays, Tuesdays and Thursdays; recent storms are provisional for one to three days, and best tracks are finalised after one to two years |
| ERA5-Land | daily precipitation per unit | daily, typically about five days behind |
| Groundsource | polygons of places named in news reports about flooding, overlaid on each unit | covers 2000-01-01 to 2026-01-22 |
| GHSL | population and population-weighted unit centroids | one population file per year |
| geoBoundaries | ADM2 units, their names and boundaries | one set of units for all years |

G-TROPIC itself is rebuilt every Sunday at about 02:00 (New York time). It is
published as two Harvard Dataverse datasets: a historical one, covering 1980
to the previous calendar year and revised about once a year, and a
current-year one, updated weekly. Both are versioned, so any published version
can be retrieved again (`vignette("versions-and-caching", package = "gtropic")`).

Groundsource ([Mayo et al., 2026](https://doi.org/10.31223/X5RR2K), a
preprint) is a dataset of flood events extracted from news articles: an AI
model reads each article, picks out the place and date of the flooding, and
looks up that place's boundary on Google Maps. A flood polygon is therefore
the outline of a place named in a news report, which can be a street or a
whole province, not a map of where the water was. As noted by Groundsource,
flood data is both spatially and temporally biased: floods in regions and
periods with more accurate reporting are over-represented, and those lacking
news coverage are under-represented. `?gtropic_known_limitations` explains
what the flood values measure, and why gtropic returns three flood columns
under names other than the published ones.

Every result records these schedules and the period it covers;
`gtropic_availability()` returns them. A query that reaches the most recent
storms, the last few days of precipitation or the end of the flood record
warns about it, and the warnings are kept with the result
(`gtropic_diagnostics()`).

## What is available

Filters that match nothing are errors, not empty results, so it helps to look
values up first. The helpers download only small metadata files.

```{r}
library(gtropic)

# Genesis years in the historical and current-year datasets
gtropic_years()

# Administrative units, optionally restricted to a country
gtropic_adm2()
gtropic_adm2(WHO_ENTITY = "United States")

# Storms that formed in 2025, or one storm by its convenience label
gtropic_storms(date_range = 2025)
gtropic_storms(STORM_NAME = "Katrina-2005")

# Storms excluded from the published wind data
gtropic_excluded_storms(date_range = 2025)
```

`STORM_GENESIS_DATE_UTC`, the date of a storm's first best-track
observation, is the date every temporal filter uses, and the yearly storm,
wind, zero-pair and track files are organised by its calendar year. A
`STORM_NAME` such as `"Katrina-2005"` can match more than one storm, and its
year is the published `SEASON`, which can differ from the genesis year; query
by the unique `STORM_ID` instead.

## What the columns mean

The codebook documents every table and column: what it measures, its units,
and the source and pipeline step that produced it. Three flood columns are
returned under other names than the codebook's (see "Flood columns" in
`?gtropic_data`). `gtropic_metrics()` lists
the exposure metrics that `gtropic_plot()` can map, with their units and
default aggregation.

```{r}
codebook <- gtropic_codebook()
names(codebook)

gtropic_metrics()
```
